---
name: Propose a pattern
about: Something you keep doing that the catalogue has no name for
title: "Pattern: <plain name>"
labels: pattern proposal
---

New patterns start here rather than as a pull request, and CONTRIBUTING.md says
why: an entry is a signed, dated claim, and it is refusable because one person is
accountable for what it says. Almost nothing here is formally verified, and that is fine — what matters is that you have seen it. If
this lands it gets written into the paper it belongs to, and you are credited
for the proposal.

**The forces** — what pulls against what. A pattern that resolves no tension is
a tip rather than a pattern.

**Where you have seen it**, and how often. Existence beats frequency here; both
beat plausibility.

**The cost.** An entry with only benefits has not been used in anger.

**How you would know this is unnecessary** — the condition that would make the
pattern pointless, named precisely enough to check. This is the hardest field
and the most valuable.

**Where it sits** — which of the six sections, and what it relates to. "A new
section" is a legitimate and more interesting answer.
